column1: Alternatively expressed, the government cannot engineer a permanent tax cut unless government expenditures are also cut (in present value terms). Because the fiscal theory of the price level assumes that (4.37) holds only when evaluated at the equilibrium price level, the government can plan a permanent tax cut. If it does, the price level must rise to ensure that the new, lower value of discounted surpluses is again equal to the real value of government debt. For (4.39) to define an equilibrium price level, it must hold that Dt 0 0. Niepelt (2004) argued that the fiscal theory cannot hold if there is no initial outstanding stock of nominal government debt. However, Daniel (2007) showed that one can define non-Ricardian policies in a consistent manner when the initial stock of debt is zero.
